body:
The Dockerfile removes two trees that `COPY . /app/calibre-web-automated/`
(STEP 6) brought in: `frontend/` in the RUN right after the COPY, and
`koreader/` at the end of STEP 7 (#1478). Neither reclaims anything.

`docker history` on the published image shows the COPY as its own 61.8 MB
layer. A path removed in any later layer is only whiteout-ed: the bytes stay
in the COPY layer and are still pulled and still stored on disk. Both removals
make the path invisible inside a running container, which is worth having, but
neither is a size win, and the frontend/ comment already says it "should be in
.dockerignore".

To actually drop them, either add them to `.dockerignore` (frontend/ cannot be,
it is consumed by STAGE 0 from the build context) or restructure so the final
stage `COPY --from=`s only what it needs — for koreader/ that is just
`koplugin.zip` into `cps/static/`.

Not urgent: the combined saving is ~188 KB for koreader/ plus whatever
frontend/ weighs, against a 61.8 MB layer. Worth folding into a future pass
that reworks the COPY/stage layout rather than doing on its own.
title: Deleting a COPYed path in a later RUN layer never reclaims image bytes
